counterexamples: N(D(x)) and D(N(x)) are distinct tree-rule irreducibles and evaluate equally on every integer
lean_reference: BTCalculus.Rewrite.rewrite_N_D proves the integer identity; in that system it was not a tree rule
notes: Unique syntactic NF of the tree TRS without N(D)→D(N) is a different claim and is proved (BTC-op-fragment-nf). This entry only refutes semantic canonicity of those irreducibles. After adding N(D)→D(N) as a tree rule the twins join; that enlarged claim is op_fragment_nd_semantic / BTC-op-fragment-nd-semantic.
statement: Without N(D(x))→D(N(x)) as a tree rule, irreducibles of the operator fragment {D, I_a, S, N} are unique representatives of integer functions.
tested_range: exact identity N∘D = D∘N; probe set n in [-30, 30] in tests/unit/test_operator_fragment_nf.py
title: Operator-fragment tree NF is a unique semantic representative
